input: Research paid parental leave policies at my company

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Parental leave policies can vary by leave type (birth, adoption, foster), employee type (full-time, part-time, contractor), and whether the user wants to understand the full policy or just a specific aspect like pay rate or duration.

The policy details that matter most depend on who is taking leave — a primary caregiver vs. secondary caregiver often have very different entitlements, and the user's role or tenure may affect eligibility.
Whether the user is actively planning to take leave soon or just doing early exploratory research changes how urgent and deep the research needs to be.
The user may have a specific timeline — e.g., a baby due in a few months — which creates a hard deadline for when this information must be gathered and acted on.
Knowing where to look (HR portal, employee handbook, direct HR contact, manager) determines the immediate first action and how easy the research will be.

The user may simply want a summary of what they're entitled to, or they may need a full comparison of policy options, or they may want to identify gaps to negotiate — this shapes how thorough the output needs to be.
The user may prefer to research quietly on their own (e.g., not ready to tell their employer) vs. being comfortable asking HR directly, which significantly changes the research approach.

gold.taskTitle: Research paid parental leave policies at your company
gold.taskDescription: Find and understand the paid parental leave policies that apply to the user at their current employer.

questions.title: Which type of leave are you researching — birth, adoption, or foster?
questions.description: Identify the specific parental leave scenario so the research focuses on the right policy category, as entitlements often differ significantly by leave type.

questions.title: Are you the primary or secondary caregiver in this situation?
questions.description: Determine the caregiver role, since most companies offer different durations and pay rates for primary vs. secondary caregivers.

questions.title: Is this for imminent planning, or early exploratory research?
questions.description: Understand the urgency of the research to calibrate how quickly and thoroughly the information needs to be gathered.

questions.title: Do you have a specific leave start date or due date in mind?
questions.description: A known timeline creates a hard deadline for completing the research and initiating any required HR processes before leave begins.

questions.title: Do you know where your company stores its leave policy documents?
questions.description: Identify the starting point for research — HR portal, employee handbook, intranet, or direct HR contact — to determine the immediate next action.

questions.title: What does a useful outcome look like — a quick summary or a detailed breakdown?
questions.description: Clarify the depth of output needed, whether a simple overview of entitlements or a thorough breakdown covering pay, duration, eligibility, and process steps.

questions.title: Are you comfortable asking HR directly, or do you prefer researching privately?
questions.description: Understand the user's comfort level with visibility, since this determines whether the research strategy relies on self-serve documents or direct conversations with HR or a manager.
